drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur des premières lignes, un cercle tracé à main levée ; du centre partent deux rayons, vers le haut à droite et vers le bas à droite, chacun doublé d'un trait pointillé, et un court trait horizontal portant un point : le secteur $-\theta \leq \arg z \leq +\theta$.
drawings.kind: circle with a sector (two radii and the axis)
drawings.notes: Left margin, beside the first lines. A freehand closed curve, egg-shaped and open at the left, its upper left arc heavy (traced through points of the page); from a centre slightly above the middle, two radii to the upper right and to the lower right, ending on the curve; each radius has a row of dots or short dashes beside it, on the side of the sector; a short thin horizontal stroke to the right of the centre, with one dot on it. It is the sector -theta <= arg z <= +theta of the text. Disagreement in part with the note of the transcription (« trois rayons … découpant le disque en trois secteurs, deux des rayons pointillés »): the two oblique radii are solid lines doubled by dots, the third stroke is a short axis that does not reach the circle. Still differs: the upper radius is thin and its dotted double heavy, the lower radius heavy and its dots light; both pairs are drawn alike. Nothing struck. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the outline is not a circle (it is wider at the top, flattened at the lower right, with a gap at the left); drawn before as a circle, up to 3 units off; now traced through points of the page, and the ends of the radii moved onto it. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
drawings.disagreement: The note says three radii cutting the disc into three sectors, two of them dotted; the page shows two solid radii, each doubled by a dotted line, and a short horizontal axis with a point, which stops well inside the circle.
